  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  January 13, 2025
  6:00 p.m.
ROLL CALL: At 6:34 p.m., on Monday, January 13, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Deputy Director of Public Works and Utilities
Ramos, Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services
LohGuan, Director of Human Resources Ko, Battalion Chief Brown, Economic Development Specialist
Chew, Manager Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Wang

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

WANG: Mayor WANG provided a brief update on the recent windstorm and Eaton Fire incident that
impacted the community. She extended heartfelt gratitude to City staff including first responders,
Public Works, Utilities, and Parks and Recreation. She briefly described the type of work performed
by staff and their contributions. Ms. Wang also recognized the Library staff for opening Reese Hall to
FEMA staff who provided assistance to those in need. She went on to provide updates to City Services
such as parking restrictions, waste removal, water qualities and services, and use of power leaf
blowers. She further provided information to the public regarding emergency notifications and alerts.
Ms. Wang stated that recent events served as reminders to revisit the City’s emergency preparedness
plan and to strengthen neighborhood watch programs. She assured the public that the City was
prepared to respond to any emergencies.

CEREMONIAL

1.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: DIANE DELGADILLO-JIMENEZ – F2M25-3

  Mayor Wang and the City Council wished to commend and thank Police Clerk Diane
  Delgadillo-Jimenez for her 36 years of faithful and loyal service to the Police Department and
  the City of Alhambra. Mayor Wang presented a Certificate of Service plaque to Ms.
  Delgadillo-Jimenez for her outstanding work for the City.

  Ms. DELGADILLO-JIMENEZ expressed gratitude for the City and her coworkers during her
  years of service.

 PRESENTATIONS

2.  APPROVE CITY COUNCIL APPOINTMENTS – F2M24-38, M2M25-1

  City Clerk MYLES delivered a staff report. At the December 9, 2024 Council meeting, the
  Council adopted a resolution which declared Jeff Maloney elected as Councilperson of the
  Third District and Noya Wang elected as Councilperson of the Fourth District. Additionally,
  Noya Wang became Mayor, by virtue of being elected to the Fourth District, replacing the
  outgoing Councilmember and current Mayor, Sasha Renée Pérez. Due to the restructuring of
  the City Council, vacancies were created for positions on various external boards/commissions
  that should now be filled. A list reflecting all of the current City Council appointments as well
  as vacancies was prepared by staff.

  Discussion: Mayor WANG requested to serve on the Board of Directors for the League of
  California Cities, San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments – Transportation Committee, and
  the Southern California Association of Governments. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER
  nominated herself to be an alternate member to the Alhambra Historical Museum Board of
  Directors. Hearing no other nominations, Mayor Wang nominated herself as the alternate
  member for the Independent Cities Association.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to approve all nominations for vacancies as well as the
  other current City Council appointments as outlined in the January 13, 2025 staff report by the
  City Clerk.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the nomination of Mayor Wang as a member to
  the Board of Directors, League of California Cities, the representative to the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments – Transportation Committee, the representative to the Southern
  California Association of Governments, and the alternate representative to the Independent
  Cities Association; the nomination of Councilmember Andrade-Stadler as the alternate
  representative to the Alhambra Historical Museum Board of Directors; along with the other
  current City Council appointments as outlined in the City Clerk’s January 13, 2025 report; and
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-1)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded: MALONEY
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

3.  SURVEY REGARDING THE AGENDA PLACEMENT OF PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-
  AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M24-7

  At the October 28, 2024 Council meeting, Vice Mayor Lee requested, and the City Council
  agreed to discuss the current order of items on the agenda, more specifically where public
  comment for non-agendized items takes place on the agenda. Staff reached out to surrounding
  cities in the area to find out where public comment for non-agendized items is placed on their
  agendas. City Clerk MYLES provided a summary of the survey results.

  Public Comment:
  1) Jennifer NG spoke in favor of public comment for non-agendized items at an earlier time during
  the City Council meeting.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the meeting structures of the Los Angeles
  County Board of Supervisors and South Pasadena.

  2
1-13-25
   3) Olga MICHAELS spoke in favor of public comment for non-agendized items at the beginning
  of the meeting.

  4) Randi KAYE (via Zoom) spoke in favor of public comment for non-agendized items at the
  beginning of the meeting. Ms. Kaye also praised City staff for their efforts after the recent
  windstorm.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor LEE discussed her reasons for requesting the agenda item such
  as greater accessibility to the public. She stated that she was in favor of Public Comment for
  Non-Agendized Items at the beginning or middle of the meeting. Councilmember MAZA
  supported Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items at the beginning or middle of the meeting
  but added that it should not obstruct outside presenters. Councilmember MALONEY supported
  Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items set to a time certain such as 30 minutes, and then
  continue any additional public commenters at the end of the meeting. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion to allow for public comment for
  non-agendized items for 30 minutes at the beginning of the meeting and then continue any
  additional comments at the end of the meeting. She made a motion for the same. Mayor
  WANG echoed her colleagues support for more meaningful public engagement but cautioned
  that moving public comment to the beginning may also delay speakers on agendized items.
  She therefore supported setting Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items to a time certain of
  30 minutes. She added that should the public have any needs for accommodations, they
  should reach out to Council.

  City Attorney MONTES clarified the current ordinance regarding agenda order, the need to
  approve an ordinance with any changes to that order, and suggested that before altering the
  Alhambra Municipal Code, Council could temporarily change the agenda order for a trial period
  and then request staff return with an ordinance for discussion or approval. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER clarified that the Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items would take place at the
  beginning of the meeting, but after ceremonial items. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER altered her
  previous motion to temporarily move Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items to after
  ceremonial items for an initial timeframe of no more than 30 minutes for a period of 3 months
  after which staff would return with a report on progress. Mr. MAZA suggested that the trial
  period be set to 6 months or before summer. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER agreed to the
  amendment.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed that the Agenda Item of Public Comment for Non-
  Agendized Items be temporarily set to the beginning of the meeting, after any Ceremonial
  items, for an initial set time of 30 minutes for a 6-month period; and directed staff return with a
  report after the 6 -month period.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4 – 14)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine and will
be enacted by one motion.

4.  AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR THE DESIGN AND PURCHASE OF ALHAMBRA
  PLACEMAKING SIGNAGE AND APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS FROM THE ARTS AND
  PUBLIC PLACES FUND – F2M24-51, N2M24-117, C2M25-1, M2M25-2

1-13-25
   On September 23, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for
  the Design and Purchase of Alhambra Placemaking Signage. Alhambra Placemaking signs
  would be located at Alhambra, Almansor and Granada parks. On Thursday, November 7,
  2024, the City Clerk received three bids for the Design and Purchase of Alhambra
  Placemaking Signage. The bid received from Square Signs LLC dba Front Signs was the
  lowest responsive bid. The project would be funded with Arts and Public Places funds.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Square Signs LLC dba Front Signs in an amount not to
  exceed $159,665.55 for the Design and Purchase of Alhambra Placemaking Signage;
  appropriated $159,665.55 in revenue and expenditure funds from the Arts and Public Places
  Fund; authorized the City Manager, or designee, to execute all documents related to the Public
  Works Contract; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the City
  Council's action. (M2M25-2)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE

5.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION PROCLAIMING THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY DUE TO WINDSTORM EVENT – F2M25-20, R2M25-1

  Staff requested that the City Council adopt a resolution proclaiming the existence of a Local
  Emergency due to the recent windstorm and extreme fire weather. The weather system and
  wind event caused extreme conditions such as power outages, damage to power poles,
  utilities infrastructure and fallen trees, impacting transportation arteries and requiring repair.
  There existed a need to protect the health, safety and welfare of the residents and property of
  the City of Alhambra and conditions warrant and necessitated that the City of Alhambra declare
  the existence of a local emergency.

  Public Comment:
  1) Jennifer NG expressed gratitude to Alhambra Fire, Police, Public Works, and other staff for
  their quick response and work during the recent windstorm. She suggested publicizing
  additional contact information for minor issues during emergencies.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., thanked the City Manager and staff for the resolution.
  He read portions of the Resolution and discussed the potential for Federal reimbursement. He
  also praised City staff for their work clearing fallen trees after the windstorm. He went on to
  discuss the older light structures that needed repair.

  3) Olga MICHAELS thanked the City and praised staff for their work. She added that she looked
  forward to updates to the emergency preparedness plan, requested that the City ensure that
  all fire hydrants were functional, requested education for the public on how to turn off their gas,
  requested more CERT classes, and requested that all downed trees be replaced.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked the City Manager for the
  resolution, thanked staff for their quick response and for the information provided on social
  media, she also thanked Public Works for quick clean up, thanked the Library for distributing
  masks and allowing a place for FEMA services, thanked the Police Department for their
  patrols, and thanked the Fire Department for their work during the fires. She expressed
  sympathy to all those who lost their homes.

  4
1-13-25
   Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-1 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, proclaiming the
  existence of a Local Emergency

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

6.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ONE FULL ELECTRIC PICKUP TRUCK FOR THE
  ALHAMBRA UTILITIES DEPARTMENT – F2M25-6A, C2M25-2, M2M25-3

  As part of the City of Alhambra’s ongoing effort to develop a greener and more energy-efficient
  fleet, staff recommended the purchase of one fully electric pickup truck. This zero-emissions
  vehicle would replace an aging service truck that has been in use for 10 years. Staff aimed to
  acquire this new electric pickup truck through a cooperative purchase agreement, ensuring a
  sustainable upgrade to the City’s vehicle fleet. Cooperative purchase is allowable per
  Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On February 8, 2024, Sourcewell opened bids for
  procuring cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with related equipment, accessories, and
  services. Sourcewell awarded contract 032824-NAF to National Auto Fleet Group on July 2,
  2024, an agreement that would not expire until July 9, 2028. Staff recommended purchasing
  one truck under this option.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the purchase of one full
  electric pickup truck in the amount of $59,235.76; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-3)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ONE UTILITY SERVICE TRUCK FOR THE
  UTILITIES DEPARTMENT – F2M25-6A, C2M25-3, M2M25-4

  The 2024-25 Fiscal Year Budget included the replacement of one utility service body truck.
  The existing utility truck was over 10 years old and reached its end of service life. The truck
  would be utilized for on-call in the Water Division. As such, staff sought to purchase a service
  body truck to replace the vehicle through a cooperative purchase agreement. Cooperative
  purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On February 8, 2024,
  Sourcewell opened four bids for procuring vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with
  related equipment, accessories, and services. Sourcewell awarded contract 03824-NAF to
  National Auto Fleet Group on November 4, 2021 - an agreement that would not expire until
  July 9, 2028. Per the Sourcewell bid specifications, there is the option of purchasing vehicles
  and equipment. Staff recommended purchasing one truck under this option.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the purchase of a service

8.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN & CONSTRUCTION
  SERVICES FOR THE SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON SIERRA VISTA
AVENUE – F2M24-65, RFP2M24-24, C2M25-4, M2M25-5

  On October 14, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for professional engineering design services and construction support service for the Sewer
  Main Replacement Project on Sierra Vista Avenue. As part of the City of Alhambra’s ongoing
  Capital Improvement Program, this project provided engineering design, plans, and
  preparation of bid specifications needed for the replacement of approximately 1,065 feet of
  existing 8-inch sewer main with a larger capacity sewer main. Staff reviewed a total of four
  proposals. West & Associates Engineering Inc. was selected based on their qualifications,
  experience, reputation, responsiveness, availability, and cost.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and West &
  Associates Engineering Inc., in an amount not to exceed $57,000.00, for engineering design
  and construction support services for Sewer Main Replacement Project on Sierra Vista
  Avenue; authorized the City Manager or designee to execute all documents related to the
  contract; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action.
  (M2M25-5)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN & CONSTRUCTION
  SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON
  CONCORD AVENUE, LA PALOMA AVENUE AND MERIDIAN AVENUE – F2M24-63,
RFP2M24-22, C2M25-5, M2M25-6

  On September 23, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for the Water Main Replacement Project on Concord Avenue, La Paloma Avenue, and
  Meridian Avenue. The Utilities Department regularly installs water mains to replace aging
  pipelines and to improve system reliability and water quality. This project would replace the
  approximately 6,500 feet of 4-inch cast iron pipe on Meridian Avenue and La Paloma Avenue
  with 8-inch Ductile Iron pipe, and 830 feet of 6-inch cast iron pipe on Concord Avenue with 8-
  inch Ductile Iron pipe. Staff reviewed a total of eight proposals. Elie Farah Inc. was selected
  based on their qualifications, experience, reputation, responsiveness, availability, and cost.

  Discussion:  None.

  the Water Main Replacement Project on Concord Avenue, La Paloma Avenue, and Meridian

10.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: REHABILITATION OF THE STORM DRAIN PIPES ON
  COMMONWEALTH AVENUE AND GRAND AVENUE – F2M24-28, C2M24-47, M2M25-6

  On July 22, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to CEM Construction Corp for the
  Rehabilitation of the Storm Drain pipes on Commonwealth Avenue and Grand Avenue in the
  amount of $195,875.00. There were no change orders during the construction. However, there
  was one change order request to correct the original account number from 101.80.8676.64940
  to 233.80.8882.62210; and an appropriation of $28,191 was needed from the Safe Clean
  Water Program (SCWP) Fund to cover the remaining project balance. The project was
  completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would
  be appropriate for the City Council to accept the project as complete and instruct the City Clerk
  that the Notice of Completion be filed with the County of Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of CEM Construction Corp for the
  Rehabilitation of the Storm Drain pipes on Commonwealth Avenue and Grand Avenue as
  complete; directed the Finance Director to allocate $28,191 from the Safe Clean Water
  Program (SCWP) Fund to cover the remaining project balance; directed the City Clerk to file
  a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation; directed the Finance
  Director to release the five percent retention 35 days from the date of recordation, if no liens
  are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action.
  (M2M25-7)

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M25-4
1) Connie CERVANTES reported on the difficult parking situation on Hellman and Second streets due the
  medical building in front. She requested an established crosswalk. She also discussed issues with trash
  pickup.
  8
1-13-25
 2) Dan DUNCAN explained that he was functionally deaf and a retired Alhambra Police Department
  Sergeant. He went on to discuss the oath taken by police officers and the retirement policies for police
  officers including CCW permit. He requested his identification card and CCW permit. He distributed a
  handout to Council providing additional explanation of his case.

3) Brian LEE discussed a non-functioning street light on Montezuma Avenue and the delayed repair from
  City staff due to a personnel shortage. He requested permission to hire a private company to repair the
  street light and then for the City to reimburse him.

4) Jennifer NG requested signage at Hidalgo and Commonwealth indicating that the intersection was a 2-
  way stop. Due to the lack of Planning Commission meetings, she went on to request clarification on the
  ministerial approval of projects for the public during the annual review of the zoning code. Ms. NG also
  expressed hope that the community could come together to support neighbors in other cities who have
  lost their homes during the wildfires.

5) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., echoed Ms. Ng’s comments regarding the lack of Planning
  Commission meetings and further requested the status of development operations in the City be posted
  on the City website for the benefit of the public. He specifically requested information regarding the
  Emmaus Lutheran Church property and suggested that the area be considered for affordable housing
  development or the expansion of recreation facilities. Mr. McCammon went on to speak regarding the
  passing of former President Jimmy Carter and his many accomplishments. Mr. McCammon also
  discussed the widespread fire damage to the community in Altadena.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) – F2M25-7

Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER offered condolences to those who suffered losses due to the
recent wildfires. She requested more information regarding online notifications and requests for City
services. City Manager BINNQUIST provided information regarding online service requests via the City
website and outlined the City’s discussions with Southern California Edison regarding street light
service.

Councilmember MALONEY offered condolences for those who suffered losses due to the recent
wildfires and discussed the volunteer efforts to help those affected such as American Legion in
Alhambra and All Soul’s Church. He praised City staff for their quick response to the windstorm.

Councilmember MAZA expressed gratitude to City staff for their quick response to the windstorm and
offered condolences for those who suffered losses due to the recent wildfires. He also discussed
services offered by the American Legion post in Alhambra.

Vice Mayor LEE spoke about the effects of the windstorm and fires as well as the relative peace and
safety in Alhambra. She expressed the need to offer help in any way possible. She thanked the Fire
Departments for their work containing the wildfires. She emphasized the need for emergency
preparedness.

Mayor WANG expressed appreciation for her colleagues’ comments and further expressed gratitude
for City staff and their efforts. She also thanked her neighbors and the community for their patience
during the power outages. Ms. Wang referred to Item 3 and requested staff notify the public of the
temporary change to the Council agenda order. She also further discussed Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s
comments regarding requests for service and requested staff provide a method for tracking service
requests and notifications to the public. Ms. Wang also discussed comments regarding emergency
preparedness and requested that staff bring back the emergency preparedness plan for discussion
and review. Ms. Wang went on to discuss upcoming events such as the Lunar New Year festival.
